newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Commander of feared Zaire civil guard to head army.
newsitem.headline: Commander of feared Zaire civil guard to head army.

text.p: The commander of Zaire's feared civil guard will take over as interim chief of staff of the Central African country's army, state radio said on Thursday.
General Kpama Baramoto Kata, a close ally of President Mobutu Sese Seko, was named for the post by the defence minister to replace General Eluki Monga who was suspended on Wednesday.

Eluki's downfall came after statements he made on French radio contradicting the government's position favouring the deployment of a multinational force in Zaire to help refugees fleeing the fighting in its eastern provinces.
Eluki told French radio on Tuesday that the intervention of a U.N. force in Zaire was now unnecessary after the exodus home of nearly half a million Rwandan refugees.

A government official said Eluki also repeated complaints by the army that the government was not giving the military the means to battle Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels who have seized much of Zaire's two eastern provinces.
The Zaire government maintains that a multinational force is still needed to help hundreds of thousands of other refugees and Zairean villagers displaced by fighting since October 18.
Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo told reporters on Thursday that Eluki had overstepped his mark.
"The chief of staff should not take decisions which are the responsibility of the government," Kengo said.
The top officers in Zaire are from the same Equateur region as Mobutu or have close family ties. Baramoto who comes from the same Ngbandi ethnic group as Mobutu, was Eluki's deputy.

For more than seven years Baramoto commanded the civil guard, the most feared of Zaire's armed forces by the civilian population. Since its creation in the mid-1980s the civil guard has often been used to quash local disturbances and Baramoto's appointment is therefore unlikely to be popular.
Radical opposition activists quickly criticised Kengo's weak centrist government for reshuffling the top generals in public at a time of war.

"It's bound to demoralise the army. But I think the reason the government acted was because it was scared that Eluki might act first," Kibiswa Kwabene Naupess, deputy secretary general of the Democratic Labour Confederation said.
However, the changes in the top army ranks are unlikely to have taken place without the go-ahead from Mobutu, who has been convalescing in Europe for close to three months.
"Historically it is Mobutu who has made or marred the top generals. Even if he is abroad, it is unlikely that this time would be an exception," one Zaire analyst said.
Mobutu, who has the rank of field marshal, seized power in 1965 as a young officer and has ruled alone most of the time.
Baramoto's appointment as interim army chief of staff puts an end to rumours that General Mahele Bokungu, the most popular of the generals, would rise back to the top of the army.
